newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rally to slightly higher close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rally to slightly higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied in the final minutes of trade on Thursday to close slightly higher on buying in laggard blue chips and with sentiment again fired by red-chip fever, brokers said.
"We have a polarised market," said Keith Wu, research manager at Peregrine Securities. "There is still ample appetite for red chips while a quiet mood dominates in the blue chips."

The Hang Seng Index closed 19.79 points, or 0.16 percent, higher at 12,726.83 after trading in negative territory for most of the day. Turnover was a heavy HK$13.51 billion, higher than Wednesday's HK$9.90 billion.

Turnover was inflated by nearly HK$2.48 billion in trade in China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings, which was part of the company's HK$3.87 billion share issue of 650 million new shares. The share closed HK$1.30 higher at HK$7.85.

For most of the day, the market seemed ready to follow Wall Street's caution. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 21.87 points, or 0.31 percent, to 6,812.72 on Wednesday after soaring 173 points the day before.
But the Hang Seng reversed course in the last 30 mintues of trade, rising from 80 points down to its slightly higher close in line with Hang Seng Index futures.
The April contract closed 55 points higher at 12,725 but on sharply lower volume of 17,094 contracts.
The finance sector led the blue chips, followed by the commercial and industrial sector.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings jumped HK$1.00 to HK$190.50 on heavy trade of HK$487.95 million.

Conglomerate Swire Pacific was the best performing blue chip. The share rallied HK$1.25 to close at HK$58.00 after the company announced a property development joint venture with Sun Hung Kai Properties.
Sun Hung Kai gained HK$0.50 to HK$81.50.
Red chips led the best performers' table.
"Red chips are totally crazy," said one broker.
Red chip favourite China Resources gained HK$2.55 to HK$23.75.
Shanghai Industrial added HK$2.30 to HK$43.30. Stockbrokers Shenyin Wanguo jumped HK$0.65 to HK$2.70.
Blue chip Guangdong Investment closed HK$0.25 higher at HK$7.15 after announcing a 4.42 percent rise in earnings to HK$604.29 million in 1996.
